title: Lisse sheaves of modules are module objects in finite locally constant sheaves of sets
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite ring (not necessarily commutative). Call a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of left $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ *lisse* if there are an etale covering $\{U_i\to Y\}$ and finite left $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}_{U_i}$ as sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, where $\underline M$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $U\mapsto M$. Write $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ for the category of finite locally constant sheaves of sets on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; it has finite products (computed in all sheaves of sets) and the final object $\underline{\{*\}}$. A *$\Lambda$-module object* of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ is an object $\mathcal A$ with morphisms $+:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$, $0:\underline{\{*\}}\to\mathcal A$, $-:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $\lambda\cdot:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, satisfying the axioms of a left $\Lambda$-module written as commutative diagrams; a morphism of $\Lambda$-module objects is a morphism of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ commuting with these maps. Then:

1. A sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ is lisse if and only if its underlying sheaf of sets lies in $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$.
2. The functor sending a lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$ to its underlying sheaf of sets with the addition, zero, negation and scalar multiplications of $\mathcal F$ is an equivalence (indeed an isomorphism) from the category of lisse sheaves of left $\Lambda$-modules, with $\Lambda$-linear maps of sheaves, onto the category of $\Lambda$-module objects of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$.
